summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia and chronic tracheostomy was admitted for increased greenish tracheal secretions with blood streaks, dyspnea on exertion, chills, and odynophagia. She had multiple recent admissions with similar symptoms, none of which showed infection. Initial evaluation revealed normal vital signs, clear lungs, and a chest X-ray without acute findings. Blood cultures were negative, and early sputum samples were contaminated. A tracheal aspirate on hospital day three confirmed Staphylococcus aureus and Haemophilus influenzae, leading to a diagnosis of bacterial tracheitis. She was treated with intravenous vancomycin, which was continued at home for a full 10-day course. Her chronic pain, microcytic anemia, and GERD were managed with home medications. She improved clinically, was discharged home with visiting nurse support, and had follow-up arranged with her primary care provider and ENT.
